== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' was baptised at Kilbirnie, Ayrshire, on 01 Dec 1749. The parish register names his father as John and his mother as Margarat.<ref name="FMP1" /> Because the entry records a baptism rather than a birth, his birth is placed before that date, and Kilbirnie is inferred from the baptism rather than independently recorded.

== Research Notes ==
The baptism is the only record currently assigned to this William. The Currie entry below is a possible later record, not an established identification. A search of live WikiTree profiles found no compatible match; [[Glasgow-1124|William]] belongs to a different family and is not this person.

=== Possible Currie record, 1822 ===

A possible later record concerns William Glasgow of Ballerno, Currie, aged 72 in 1822. One Findmypast transcript labels 11 November 1822 as his death date (OPR 682/3, item 4); its Lothian companion labels that day as burial, leaves the exact death date unknown, and records a mortcloth charge of 15s (book 4, page 3). These are companion derivative transcripts, not independent witnesses.<ref name="Currie1822">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Deaths & Burials 1564-2017'': [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F1292654 William Glasgow, OPR transcript SCOT/OPR/BUR/1292654], OPR 682/3, item 4; and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FLOTHIAN%2FFHS%2FBUR%2F001369 Lothian transcript GBPRS/LOTHIAN/FHS/BUR/001369], parish 682, book 4, page 3. Both give residence Ballerno and age 72. Derivative transcripts inspected 30 October 2026; original register not inspected.</ref>

If the reported age represents completed years on 11 November 1822, it permits a birth between 12 November 1749 and 11 November 1750. That range overlaps William's birth before his 1 December 1749 baptism, so age does not exclude him. The indexed birth year 1750 is age-derived, not an independently recorded birth. Neither Currie transcript names relatives or establishes a link from the Kilbirnie child to an adult resident of Ballerno. This remains a candidate identification; no death or burial is assigned to this William. The original Currie register and evidence connecting his later household or residence are needed to resolve it.
